name: al-Khansa'
bio: Tumadir bint Amr ibn al-Harith ibn al-Sharid, of the Sulaym of Qays Aylan, was a poet of Najd; al-Khansa' is the nickname that stuck to her. Most of her life was spent before Islam; she lived to become a Muslim and came to the Prophet with her people, and al-Zirikli says he would ask her to recite and admired her verse. The greater part of her poetry, and the best of it, mourns her brothers Mu'awiya and Sakhr, both killed before Islam: the tribe of Murra killed Mu'awiya when he raided them, and Sakhr, speared in a raid on the Asad, died of the wound years later, as Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani tells. Durayd ibn al-Simma once asked to marry her, and she refused him. Al-Zirikli reports that her four sons fought at al-Qadisiyya in 16 AH (637 CE), urged on by her to stand firm until all of them were killed; she died in 24 AH (645 CE).
